PLAN "Return-to-Baseline Load Decision Guidance"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Assess readiness for immediate return to pre-illness loads"

PHASES
  PHASE "Decision Guidance" (1 week):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday education 0m "Load Progression Guidance":
        main straight_sets:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 5m rpe 0 rest 0 seconds
          plank 1x30s rpe 0 rest 0 seconds
        cooldown:
          forward_fold 1m
        notes:
          - "Despite feeling normal, rapid return to pre-illness loads after 3+ weeks off and 4kg weight loss increases risk of injury and excessive fatigue."
          - "Muscle mass, connective tissue resilience, and work capacity may not be fully restored even if subjective energy is normal."
          - "Recommended: Resume at 70..80% of pre-illness loads for compound lifts, monitor RPE and recovery, and progress weekly as tolerated."
          - "If first sessions feel easy (RPE <6), increase load by 5..10% per session until baseline is reached."
          - "Monitor for delayed onset fatigue, soreness, or performance drop-off; if present, reduce load or volume."
          - "Full return to pre-illness loads is typically safe after 1..2 weeks of progressive reintroduction, provided recovery is robust and no symptoms recur."
          - "Consult with a qualified professional if in doubt or if any symptoms return."

PLAN "Readiness Criteria for Full Intensity Return"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Identify signals for safe return to full intensity training"

PHASES
  PHASE "Readiness Assessment" (1 week):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday education 0m "Readiness Signals":
        main straight_sets:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 5m rpe 0 rest 0 seconds
        cooldown:
          forward_fold 1m
        notes:
          - "Consistent completion of all prescribed sessions at 70..85% pre-illness loads with RPE ≤7 and no excessive fatigue."
          - "No lingering or delayed muscle soreness beyond 48 hours post-session."
          - "Normal sleep quality and duration; no new sleep disturbances."
          - "Stable or increasing body weight and appetite."
          - "No recurrence of illness symptoms (fatigue, cough, fever, etc)."
          - "Normal resting heart rate and no unusual elevations during or after training."
          - "Subjective feeling of readiness and motivation to train."
          - "Ability to complete warmups and main lifts with good technique and without compensations."
          - "If all above are met for at least 1 week, gradual return to full intensity (RPE 8..9, pre-illness loads) is appropriate."
